probe.prompt: /skill:grill-me A 'snooze card' feature for our kanban board app: a user can park a card until a chosen date, it disappears from the board while snoozed, and resurfaces in its column when the date arrives.
answers: Primary actor: a single board user managing their own backlog. Scope: one board, one user view — no team/shared snooze state.
Snoozed cards must be findable: a 'Snoozed' filter or list per column. They never send notifications — resurfacing is silent.
If the card's column was deleted while snoozed, it resurfaces in the board's first column. Timezone: the user's local date, end-of-day.
Non-goals: recurring snooze, snoozing someone else's card, automation rules. Keep the smallest version that solves 'get it out of my face until then'.
Editing a snoozed card: allowed via the snoozed list; editing does not wake it. Waking early is a manual 'unsnooze' action.
A card with an open managed run must not be snoozed — the action is disabled with a reason. That decision is settled.
Yes — that's the whole scope I care about. Go ahead and close out if the frontier is empty.

probe.prompt: /skill:grill-with-docs We need to pin down a design decision: whether 'snoozed cards' in our kanban app live as a per-user overlay or as shared board state. Interview me.
answers: Snooze is per-user: my snooze must not hide the card from teammates. Shared board state stays authoritative.
Terminology: call it 'card snooze'. A snoozed card is still a card — not archived, not deleted. 'Archive' already means permanent removal.
The data lives server-side so a snooze follows the user across devices. Local-only is a non-goal.
Unsnooze triggers: manual unsnooze, or the snooze date arriving. Editing a card never wakes it.
One edge that matters: a teammate moves a snoozed card to another column — it resurfaces in the NEW column for me.

probe.prompt: /skill:ce-brainstorm Saved filter views for our kanban board: a user can save the current filter/sort combination under a name, re-apply it later, and share it with the team via a link. I need a written requirements doc at the end — a file, not just chat.
answers: The primary actor is an individual board user saving their own views. Sharing is view-only: a teammate opening the link gets the same filters applied to the same board.
Scope: filters + sort + column visibility. Card contents never change. Non-goals: permission systems, view-level edit locks, cross-board views.
A view is a named snapshot, not a live subscription — if the board's columns change later, unmatched entries are ignored, not errors.
Sharing: anyone with board access + the link. No per-view ACLs in this version.
Renaming and deleting your own views: yes. Deleting never affects the board or other users.
Success looks like: a user saves a view in under 5 seconds and a teammate opens the link and sees the identical filtered board. Keep it minimal — go with your recommendations on anything else.
Confirmed — write the requirements-only plan file now.
Yes, that scope is final. Write the file under docs/plans/.

# Saved Filter Views — requirements

## Goal Capsule
A kanban board user saves the current filter/sort/column-visibility combination as a named view, re-applies it later, and shares it via link. Teammates opening the link see the identical filtered board, read-only.

## Product Contract

### Requirements
- R1: save the board's current filter state (filter text, sort order, column visibility) under a user-chosen name.
- R2: views are per-user owned; listing shows only the user's own views plus shared ones they opened.
- R3: a shared link applies the view to the same board for any board member; read-only, never modifies the board.
- R4: views are snapshots — columns/filters that no longer exist are ignored silently.
- R5: rename and delete own views; deleting never affects the board.

### Key Decisions
- KD1 — snapshot semantics over live subscription (session-settled: user-directed). Governs R4.

### Scope Boundaries
No per-view ACLs, no cross-board views, no view-level locks, no automation triggers.

### Acceptance Examples
- AE1: user saves "bugs this week" view, reopens board a day later, applies it in one click.
- AE2: user copies the link; teammate opens it and sees the same filtered board.

answers: Stack for this scratch project: plain Vue 3 + a small Node state server with a JSON store. Board already has filter/sort state in the UI store.
Storage: a `views` table/collection keyed by board+owner; the share link is `/board/<id>?view=<viewId>` — no token auth beyond board membership.
Tests: unit tests for the serialize/apply logic and one API-flow test for save+apply+share. Keep the plan small.
Yes — proceed with your recommended structure.

# Card Tags — requirements

## Goal Capsule
Board users attach named color-coded tags to cards and filter the board by tag.

## Product Contract

### Requirements
- R1: a card carries zero or more tags; tags are per-board.
- R2: tag create/rename/delete from card or board settings; deleting a tag removes it from all cards.
- R3: board filter bar gains a tag multi-select; filtering is OR within tags.
- R4: tags render as colored chips on card fronts.

### Key Decisions
- KD1 — tags are board-scoped, not global (session-settled: user-directed). Governs R2.

### Scope Boundaries
No tag hierarchies, no cross-board tags, no tag permissions.

### Acceptance Examples
- AE1: user creates 'urgent' red tag, applies to two cards, filters board to just those cards.
- AE2: renaming a tag updates every card that carries it.

probe.prompt: /skill:brainstorming I want to add a notification center to our kanban app: an in-app inbox where card events (mentions, due dates, run completions) land, with read/unread state and per-event-type muting. This is a new subsystem — treat it as architectural work through your full process.
answers: Primary user: a board member who wants to catch up on what changed without watching the board. Events: mentions in card comments, due-date arrivals, and managed-run completions.

Sources are the app's existing domain events — the notification center subscribes to them; it does not create new event types. Delivery is in-app only: no email, no push, no websockets requirement beyond the app's existing channel.
Read/unread per event; mark-all-read per board; muting per event type per board. Retention: last 200 events per user — older ones drop silently.
Go with your recommended approach — in-process subscription over a queue table is fine if that's what you recommend.
